subject: spanish
source_note: Theme structure follows the IB Diploma Language B guide: five prescribed themes taught through receptive, productive and interactive skills. Recommended topics within each theme are taken from the guide; the IB does not prescribe them. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships (the IB does not publish these).

connections.why: Migration tests and reshapes language and identity
Lifestyle choices directly affect health and well-being
Shared beliefs and values bind communities together
Travel and tourism are products of a globalized world
Customs and traditions frame the rites that mark life stages
Personal narratives are told through and shape identity
Modern media depend on communication technology
Artistic expression reveals a culture's values and beliefs
Scientific innovation offers solutions to environmental problems
Education shapes access to the working world
Laws are the mechanism that protect human rights
Social engagement is often a drive toward greater equality
Conflict and peace-building are bound up with human rights
Reading and listening model the language students then produce
Secure grammar and vocabulary enable accurate writing and speech
The individual oral draws on theme content such as everyday life
